root = Card([header, rules, ref])
header = CardHeader("Outbox coalescing rules", "Runs on enqueue, scoped by target_id")
rules = Table([colQueued, colNew, colResult])
colQueued = Col("Queued", ["send", "send", "send", "edit", "edit", "react(add)", "read(ord=5)"])
colNew = Col("New op", ["edit", "delete", "react", "edit", "delete", "react(remove)", "read(ord=9)"])
colResult = Col("Result", ["Rewrite the send payload with the new body; one op", "Drop both; never touches the network", "Keep both, in order; the react must follow the send", "Keep the last edit", "Drop the edit, keep the delete", "Drop both (same emoji and user)", "Keep the higher ord (max-register)"])
ref = FileRef("docs/DESIGN.md", 1848, "§10.4 Outbox coalescing")
calls.text:
Outbox coalescing rules: Runs on enqueue, scoped by target_id
Queued: send, New op: edit, Result: Rewrite the send payload with the new body; one op; Queued: send, New op: delete, Result: Drop both; never touches the network; Queued: send, New op: react, Result: Keep both, in order; the react must follow the send; Queued: edit, New op: edit, Result: Keep the last edit; Queued: edit, New op: delete, Result: Drop the edit, keep the delete; Queued: react(add), New op: react(remove), Result: Drop both (same emoji and user); Queued: read(ord=5), New op: read(ord=9), Result: Keep the higher ord (max-register)
docs/DESIGN.md:1848 (§10.4 Outbox coalescing)

reply:
The table above lists all seven rules. The doc calls coalescing a **correctness requirement, not an optimization**. Without it, if you send a message offline and then edit or delete it, the queue would hold ops that point at a message ID the server has never seen. At best the server returns 404 and those ops fail. At worst they arrive out of order and leave a ghost message.

This is invariant 6 (`docs/DESIGN.md:2623`). The doc says to build it early, because adding it later means checking every op type against every other op type.
